Pursuant to the direction of Motion Bench, this matter has been notified and
thereafter has been taken up for argument.

2. Heard Mr. Ajit Kumar, learned Senior Counsel appearing for the petitioner and Mr. Vashistha,
learned Counsel for the respondent- State.
3.

The petitioner is apprehending his arrest in connection with CID P.S. Case No.30 of 2024, for the alleged offences registered under Sections 419,420,467,468,471,120(B)/34 of IPC, pending in the Court of learned AJC-XVIII-cum-Special Judge, CID, Ranchi.
4. Learned senior counsel appearing for the petitioner submits that the case is arising out of dispute of construction of building namely Ratan Heights.
5. He further submits that in the civil side, the said case gone up to the Hon'ble Supreme Court arising out of B.C. No.1049 of 2005.

6. He submits that the petitioner herein is the second builder appointed to construct the building.
The allegations are made that certain digging was made for the basement and that was said to be not in terms of the sanctioned plan.
7. He submits that certain direction was issued by the writ Court in WP(C) No.5734 of 2022 and one direction was to fill up the digging made for basement.
8. By way of referring para-22 of the petition, learned senior counsel submits that the said area has already been filled up.

He further submits that owner of the land in question has moved before this Court in ABA No.3511 of 2025 and the Coordinate Bench of this Court by the order dated 14.07.2025 has been pleased to allow the privilege of anticipatory bail to the owner of the land in question and on that ground, the petitioner may also be granted anticipatory bail.
9.
Learned counsel for the State submits that it appears that the dispute is arising out of not constructing the building in accordance with the sanctioned plan.

10. It is an admitted position that the owner of the land in question has been granted anticipatory bail in ABA No.3511 of 2025 and the Civil Writ's Court direction has been compiled by the petitioner by way of filling of the said area as disclosed in Para-22 of the Anticipatory Bail Application and the case is arising out of development agreement, the petitioner said to be the second builder for constructing of the said building.
11. Considering the facts and circumstances of this case, this anticipatory bail application is accordingly allowed.

12. The petitioner above named is directed to surrender before the learned Court within three weeks from the date of receipt of the order and on the event of his surrender / arrest, he shall be released on bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs.25,000/- (Twenty Five Thousand) with two sureties of the like amount of each to the satisfaction of learned AJC-XVIII-cum-Special Judge, CID, Ranchi, in connection with CID P.S. Case No.30 of 2024, subject to the conditions as laid under Section 482(2)
of Bhartiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023.
13.

This petition is accordingly disposed of.
(Sanjay Kumar Dwivedi, J.) R.Kumar Vijay Kumar Sahu vs The State Of Jharkhand ..... ... Opp. ... on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188308151/
